purpose: Resolve the current AUZiX package head the way Slackware/Debian-style distro builders do: select versions, resolve dependency/build chains, lock the build tree, then compile in declared order.
hard_rules: Set aside old built artifacts; do not preserve or promote them unless they pass the new substrate audit.
Do not compile anything until current-head versions, dependency chain, package chain, base substrate lock, and final compile order manifest are declared.
The only intended delta from Slackware/Debian mechanics is AUZiX path/layout policy and package metadata shape.
Base/runtime substrate packages build first and publish their runtime and development surfaces into the AUZiX native builder.
Minor-version drift is handled as a compatibility range on the selected provider, not by building parallel substrate copies.
The discovered and deduped build chain must be committed and tagged in git before any build consumes it.
Builders consume the git tag/ref that contains the lock; they do not build from an untracked dirty working tree.
Discovery/build helper tools such as jq, awk/gawk, rq, apt metadata tools, and graph/report generators belong to the build toolchain and may be used freely by the factory.
Build-toolchain helpers do not automatically become target/workstation packages unless they are explicitly selected in the target manifest.
Leaf apps build only after the native builder exposes the locked substrate headers, pkg-config files, CMake files, GIR/typelibs, schemas, and helper tools.
Leaf apps must not bundle core/security/desktop substrate libraries into app-local Libraries.
If a leaf app needs a newer substrate, stop and negotiate a new base release.

flow.description: Move or ignore previously produced package/repo artifacts from the old closure model.

stop_conditions: leaf package requires newer glibc than active base

flow.gate: Required before any compile or package build starts. The lock must be pulled back to git and tagged before builders consume it.

flow.description: Build the base substrate into the AUZiX root and AUZiX native builder container.
Build the acid/base AUZiX native container from the locked AUZiX base packages, not from Debian as a runtime universe.
From the acid/base AUZiX container, AUZiX builds AUZiX: compile app packages inside the AUZiX-native builder so they target the declared substrate.
Install into validation root/container, run CLI probes, ldd/readelf/stat/string checks, then desktop launcher checks.
